name: Tobadonijah
overview: Tobadonijah was a male Levite who served in a specific role during the reign of King Jehoshaphat. He is identified as a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat, indicating his participation in the religious or administrative duties assigned by the king. Beyond this, Scripture provides no further personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Tobadonijah means 'good [my] lord is YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's goodness and sovereignty. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:8, highlights a common biblical practice of embedding God's name within personal names to express faith and identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tobadonijah as a descendant of the tribe of Levi, identifying his tribal lineage. No other family relationships or surnames are mentioned beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Tobadonijah's significance lies in his role as a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat, which situates him within the context of religious leadership and service during a time of spiritual reform. His mention underscores the importance of Levites in supporting the king's efforts to uphold the worship of YHWH and maintain covenant faithfulness in Judah.
